question_vi: React Portal render component ở DOM khác (outside parent), nhưng event vẫn bubble qua React tree. Giải thích cơ chế này.
question_en: React Portals render a component into a different DOM location, yet events still bubble through the React tree. Explain how this works.
answer_html_vi:
createPortal(children, domNode) render children vào một DOM node khác — thoát khỏi parent về mặt DOM. Use case: modal, tooltip, dropdown cần thoát overflow: hidden hoặc context z-index của ancestor.

Điểm "ảo diệu": dù DOM tách rời, event vẫn bubble theo React tree, không theo DOM tree.

jsx
import { createPortal } from 'react-dom'

function Modal({ children, onClose }) {
  return createPortal(
    <div className="overlay" onClick={onClose}>
      <div className="modal-content">{children}</div>
    </div>,
    document.getElementById('modal-root') // DOM node khác
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <div onClick={() => console.log('App caught click')}>
      <Modal>
        <button>Click me</button>
      </Modal>
    </div>
  )
}
// → Click button trong modal VẪN log "App caught click"
// dù trong DOM, button nằm trong #modal-root, không nằm trong App

Hệ quả:
- Nên: Context, hooks, refs hoạt động bình thường qua portal (cùng React tree).
- Nên: Parent component bắt được event từ portal child — tiện cho modal close-on-overlay-click.
- Nếu cần chặn bubble lên parent, gọi e.stopPropagation() trong portal.
- Đừng nhầm: cấu trúc DOM thay đổi → CSS selector .parent .child không match nữa.
answer_html_en:
createPortal(children, domNode) renders children into a different DOM node — escaping the parent at the DOM level. Use cases: modals, tooltips, dropdowns that need to escape an ancestor's overflow: hidden or z-index context.

The "magical" part: even though the DOM is separated, events still bubble along the React tree, not the DOM tree.

jsx
import { createPortal } from 'react-dom'

function Modal({ children, onClose }) {
  return createPortal(
    <div className="overlay" onClick={onClose}>
      <div className="modal-content">{children}</div>
    </div>,
    document.getElementById('modal-root') // different DOM node
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <div onClick={() => console.log('App caught click')}>
      <Modal>
        <button>Click me</button>
      </Modal>
    </div>
  )
}
// → Clicking the button inside the modal STILL logs "App caught click"
// even though in the DOM, the button lives in #modal-root, not in App

Consequences:
- Do: Context, hooks, refs work normally through portals (same React tree).
- Do: Parent components catch events from portal children — convenient for "close modal on overlay click".
- To stop bubbling to the parent, call e.stopPropagation() inside the portal.
- Watch out: the DOM structure differs → CSS selectors like .parent .child no longer match.
